newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria president seeks Paris Club rescheduling.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria president seeks Paris Club rescheduling.

text.p: Bulgaria's President Zhelyu Zhelev on Friday proposed seeking a debt rescheduling from the Paris Club of government creditors to help the country get economic reform on track.

"It is very important for our country to seek suitable measures for financial alleviation, for example possible rescheduling of payments to the Paris Club," Zhelev said after meeting ambassadors of the G-7 countries and Russia.
He told reporters the currency board system proposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had many risks and would need support from abroad if it was to succeed.
"It is extremely important for us to secure the support -- financial, political and moral support -- of the governments of the G-7 group and Russia," he said.
"Setting up a currency board does not mean just voting a law and passing a package of measures, it means parallel implementation of structural reform and privatisation, which needs more funds."
An IMF mission last week proposed a currency board to stabilise the economy by curbing inflation and restoring confidence in the lev.
Under the scheme, the amount of levs in circulation would have to be exactly matched by the central bank's hard currency reserves.
Currency boards, pegging the local currency usually to the dollar, have been used by Argentina and the Baltic states to restore confidence and help defeat hyperinflation.
Bulgaria owes about $2 billion of its $10 billion foreign debt to the Paris Club.
Zhelev is due to leave office in January and hand over to Petar Stoyanov, also from the Union of Democratic Forces, who won elections on November 3.
Introduction of a currency board must be approved by parliament, which is dominated by the Bulgarian Socialist Party, whose leader, Prime Minister Zhan Videnov, supports the proposal.
